clauses.title: Location of phi; subcontractors - Flow-Down
clauses.text: Flow-Down. In accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.308(b)(2), Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor agrees in writing, prior to any access to PHI, to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA. Business Associate shall provide a copy of each such agreement to Covered Entity upon request.

clauses.title: Location of phi; subcontractors
clauses.text: Business Associate shall remain fully responsible for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors as if they were Business Associate's own.

clauses.title: Reporting of privacy events - Notice
clauses.text: Notice. Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity's Privacy Officer by telephone and in writing of any Privacy Event within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery. A Privacy Event shall be deemed discovered on the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, agent or Subcontractor of Business Associate.

clauses.title: Reporting of privacy events - Content
clauses.text: Content. Business Associate's notice shall include, to the extent known, the information described at 45 C.F.R. § 164.410(c), and Business Associate shall supplement such notice within five (5) days and thereafter as information becomes available.

clauses.title: Reporting of privacy events - Unsuccessful Attempts
clauses.text: Unsuccessful Attempts. Notice is hereby deemed given for unsuccessful Security Incidents, such as pings, port scans and denied log-in attempts, that do not result in unauthorized access, use or disclosure of PHI.

clauses.title: Reporting of privacy events - Cooperation
clauses.text: Cooperation. Business Associate shall cooperate fully in Covered Entity's investigation of any Privacy Event and shall not notify any Individual, regulator or media outlet of a Privacy Event without Covered Entity's prior written consent, except as Required By Law.

clauses.title: Reporting of privacy events - Mitigation
clauses.text: Mitigation. Business Associate shall promptly mitigate, at its own expense, any harmful effect of a Privacy Event.

clauses.title: Individual rights
clauses.text: Within five (5) business days of Covered Entity's request, Business Associate shall make PHI maintained in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity as necessary to satisfy 45 C.F.R. § 164.524, including in electronic form where requested.

clauses.title: Individual rights
clauses.text: Within five (5) business days of Covered Entity's request, Business Associate shall incorporate any amendment to PHI in a Designated Record Set as directed by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526.

clauses.title: Individual rights
clauses.text: Business Associate shall document disclosures of PHI and provide to Covered Entity, within ten (10) business days of request, the information required for an accounting of disclosures under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528.

clauses.title: Individual rights
clauses.text: Business Associate shall forward to Covered Entity within three (3) business days any request received directly from an Individual.

clauses.title: Compliance and audit - HHS Access
clauses.text: HHS Access. Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining Covered Entity's compliance with HIPAA.

clauses.title: Compliance and audit - Covered Entity Audit
clauses.text: Covered Entity Audit. Covered Entity or its designee may inspect and audit Business Associate's and any Subcontractor's facilities, systems, books, records, policies and procedures relating to PHI upon forty-eight (48) hours' notice, at any time during the term of this BAA and for so long as Business Associate retains any PHI. Business Associate shall promptly remediate any deficiency identified.

clauses.title: Compliance and audit - Texas Privacy Law
clauses.text: Texas Privacy Law. Business Associate shall comply with Texas Privacy Law to the extent applicable to Business Associate, including training requirements for employees who handle PHI.

clauses.title: Compliance and audit - Litigation Support
clauses.text: Litigation Support. Business Associate shall make itself and its workforce reasonably available to Covered Entity, at no cost, to testify in any litigation or administrative proceeding against Covered Entity relating to Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI, except where Business Associate is a named adverse party.

clauses.title: Indemnification; insurance - Indemnification
clauses.text: Indemnification. Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA by Business Associate or any Subcontractor; or (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law by Business Associate or any Subcontractor, including without limitation regulatory fines, civil monetary penalties, costs of notification of Individuals, regulators and media, call-center support, credit monitoring and identity theft protection for affected Individuals, forensic investigation, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

clauses.title: Indemnification; insurance - No Limitation
clauses.text: No Limitation. The obligations of Business Associate under this Article 8 are not subject to any limitation or exclusion of liability, and shall apply notwithstanding any limitation of liability in the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Indemnification; insurance - Insurance
clauses.text: Insurance. Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered Entity as an additional insured.

clauses.title: Obligations of covered entity
clauses.text: Covered Entity shall notify Business Associate of (a) any limitation in its notice of privacy practices under 45 C.F.R. § 164.520; (b) any change in, or revocation of, an Individual's authorization to use or disclose PHI; and (c) any restriction on the use or disclosure of PHI agreed to by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.522, in each case to the extent it may affect Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI.

clauses.title: Obligations of covered entity
clauses.text: Covered Entity shall not request Business Associate to use or disclose PHI in any manner that would not be permissible under HIPAA if done by Covered Entity, except as permitted by Section 2.2.

clauses.title: Obligations of covered entity
clauses.text: Covered Entity shall provide PHI to Business Associate only through the secure transfer methods or Client-controlled environments specified in Exhibit B to the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Ownership of phi; electronic transactions
clauses.text: As between the Parties, all PHI and all data derived from PHI is and shall remain the sole property of Covered Entity. Business Associate acquires no right, title or interest in PHI by reason of this BAA or the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Ownership of phi; electronic transactions
clauses.text: To the extent Business Associate conducts any Standard Transaction on behalf of Covered Entity, Business Associate shall comply with 45 C.F.R. Part 162 and shall require any Subcontractor to do the same.

clauses.title: Ownership of phi; electronic transactions
clauses.text: Business Associate shall not use PHI, or any data derived from PHI, to train, tune or evaluate any machine learning or artificial intelligence model other than models developed exclusively for Covered Entity under the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Ownership of phi; electronic transactions
clauses.text: Business Associate shall maintain policies and procedures, and documentation of all actions and assessments required by Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164, for six (6) years from the later of creation or last effective date, and shall make them available to Covered Entity on request.

clauses.title: Limited Data Sets
clauses.text: If Covered Entity provides Business Associate with a Limited Data Set, as defined at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e)(2), Business Associate shall (a) use or disclose the Limited Data Set only for the Services; (b) not identify or attempt to identify the information or contact any Individual; (c) use appropriate safeguards to prevent other use or disclosure; and (d) ensure that any Subcontractor to whom it provides the Limited Data Set agrees to the same restrictions. This Section constitutes a data use agreement for purposes of 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e)(4).

clauses.title: Term and termination - Term
clauses.text: Term. This BAA shall become effective on the Effective Date of the Master Services Agreement and shall remain in effect until all PHI provided by Covered Entity to Business Associate, or created, received or maintained by Business Associate or any Subcontractor on behalf of Covered Entity, has been returned to Covered Entity or destroyed and such return or destruction has been certified in writing by Business Associate, regardless of the expiration or termination of the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Termination for Breach
clauses.text: Termination for Breach. If Covered Entity determines that Business Associate has violated a material term of this BAA, Covered Entity may, at its option, (a) provide Business Associate an opportunity to cure within a period specified by Covered Entity, and terminate this BAA and the Master Services Agreement if Business Associate does not cure; or (b) immediately terminate this BAA and the Master Services Agreement if cure is not possible.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Return or Destruction
clauses.text: Return or Destruction. Upon termination or expiration of the Master Services Agreement, Business Associate shall, within thirty (30) days, return or destroy all PHI, including PHI in the possession of Subcontractors, retain no copies, and certify destruction in writing. If return or destruction is infeasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to such PHI and limit further uses and disclosures to those purposes that make return or destruction infeasible.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Survival
clauses.text: Survival. Articles 5, 7, 8, 10 and 11 shall survive any expiration or termination of this BAA or the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Amendment
clauses.text: Amendment. The Parties shall take such action as is necessary to amend this BAA to comply with any change in HIPAA. Covered Entity may amend this BAA by written notice to the extent required to comply with HIPAA.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Interpretation
clauses.text: Interpretation. Any ambiguity in this BAA shall be resolved to permit Covered Entity to comply with HIPAA. In the event of any conflict between this BAA and the Master Services Agreement with respect to PHI, this BAA shall control.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - No Third-Party Beneficiaries
clauses.text: No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Nothing in this BAA confers any rights upon any person other than the Parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Injunctive Relief
clauses.text: Injunctive Relief. Business Associate acknowledges that any breach of this BAA may cause Covered Entity irreparable harm, and that Covered Entity shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief without posting bond.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Governing Law
clauses.text: Governing Law. This BAA shall be governed by the laws of the State of Texas and applicable federal law, and venue shall lie as provided in the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Notices
clauses.text: Notices. Notices under this BAA shall be given as provided in the Master Services Agreement, with a copy of any notice under Article 5 to: Privacy Officer, Harrington Health Systems, Inc., 6400 Fannin Street, Suite 1800, Houston, Texas 77030 (privacy@harringtonhealth.org; Privacy Hotline (713) 555-0148).

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Relationship
clauses.text: Relationship. Business Associate is an independent contractor and is not an agent of Covered Entity for purposes of 45 C.F.R. § 160.402(c) or otherwise.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Regulatory References
clauses.text: Regulatory References. A reference in this BAA to a section of HIPAA means the section as in effect or as amended, and for which compliance is required.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Severability
clauses.text: Severability. If any provision of this BAA is held invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

clauses.title: Miscellaneous - Counterparts
clauses.text: Counterparts. This BAA may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature, and shall be executed concurrently with the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Preamble
clauses.text:
*(Client draft received 2026-09-15 via Karandeep's email. Client's paper — AtliQ has not yet marked up.)*
TravelHub FZ-LLC × AtliQ
This Software Development and Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of  2026 (the "Effective Date").

clauses.title: Parties
clauses.text: TravelHub FZ-LLC, a free zone limited liability company licensed by the Dubai Development Authority under licence no. 104772, with its office at Office 1408, Building 3, Dubai Internet City, P.O. Box 502211, Dubai, United Arab Emirates ("TravelHub" or "Customer"); and

clauses.title: Parties
clauses.text: AtliQ Inc, a Delaware corporation, with its principal office at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, NJ 08540, USA ("AtliQ" or "Developer").

clauses.title: Recitals
clauses.text:
A. TravelHub operates a consumer travel planning app and web platform ("TravelHub App") that helps travellers in the Middle East plan trips, build itineraries, and book hotels, experiences and transfers with TravelHub's partners.
B. TravelHub wishes to engage AtliQ to design and build certain AI-driven features for the TravelHub App, and AtliQ is willing to do so on the terms set out below.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Partner Hotels" means hotels, resorts and serviced apartments that have entered into a commercial or commission agreement with TravelHub for the listing and booking of their inventory through the TravelHub App.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Deliverables" means the software modules, models, APIs, source code, documentation and other work product described in Clause 4 and Schedule A.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Customer Data" means all data provided by TravelHub or generated by users of the TravelHub App, including booking history, search behaviour and user profiles.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Acceptance" means TravelHub's written confirmation that a Deliverable meets the acceptance criteria in Schedule A.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Background Technology" means software, tools and know-how owned by AtliQ prior to the Effective Date or developed independently of this Agreement.

clauses.title: Scope of work
Scope of work
clauses.text: The initial launch markets for the Partner Hotel Ranking Module shall be Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh and Jeddah, with further cities in the UAE and KSA to be added by configuration.

clauses.title: Scope of work
clauses.text: AtliQ shall provide a technical lead and a team of engineers of appropriate seniority. AtliQ's team may work remotely but shall be available for a daily stand-up during Gulf Standard Time business hours.

clauses.title: Scope of work
clauses.text: TravelHub shall provide access to its cloud environment, API documentation, historical booking data and a product owner with decision-making authority.

clauses.title: Timeline and acceptance
clauses.text: AtliQ shall use commercially reasonable efforts to meet the indicative timeline in Schedule A.

clauses.title: Timeline and acceptance
clauses.text: TravelHub shall review each Deliverable within ten (10) business days of delivery and either confirm Acceptance or provide a written list of material non-conformities. If TravelHub fails to respond within such period, the Deliverable shall be deemed accepted.

clauses.title: Timeline and acceptance
clauses.text: AtliQ shall correct any notified non-conformity and re-submit the Deliverable within a reasonable time.

clauses.title: Fees
clauses.text: The total fixed fee for the Services is USD 52,000 (fifty-two thousand US dollars), payable in instalments as set out in Schedule B.

clauses.title: Fees
clauses.text: The fees are exclusive of any applicable value added tax, which, if applicable, shall be charged in addition.

clauses.title: Fees
clauses.text: Reasonable pre-approved travel expenses, if any, shall be reimbursed at cost.

clauses.title: Invoicing and payment
clauses.text: Invoices under this Agreement shall be raised by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, GSTIN 27AAKCA4821F1Z3, on or after Acceptance of each milestone as set out in Schedule B.

clauses.title: Invoicing and payment
clauses.text: TravelHub shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days of the invoice date by wire transfer to the bank account specified on the invoice.

clauses.title: Invoicing and payment
clauses.text: Late payments shall bear interest at the rate of one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower.

clauses.title: Invoicing and payment
clauses.text: Each Party shall bear its own bank charges.

clauses.title: Term and termination
clauses.text: This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues until completion of the Services and final payment, unless terminated earlier.

clauses.title: Term and termination
clauses.text: Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure within thirty (30) days.

clauses.title: Term and termination
clauses.text: TravelHub may terminate for convenience with thirty (30) days' written notice and shall pay for all work performed up to the termination date.

clauses.title: Term and termination
clauses.text: On termination, AtliQ shall deliver all completed and in-progress Deliverables to TravelHub.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: Each Party agrees to keep the other's non-public business, technical and financial information confidential and use it solely for the purposes of this Agreement.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: These obligations do not apply to information that is publicly available, independently developed, or lawfully received from a third party.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: This Clause survives for three (3) years after termination.

clauses.title: Intellectual property
clauses.text: Upon full payment, TravelHub shall own all right, title and interest in the Deliverables developed specifically for TravelHub, including the trained models and model weights for the Itinerary Personalization Engine and Partner Hotel Ranking Module.

clauses.title: Intellectual property
clauses.text: AtliQ retains ownership of its Background Technology and grants TravelHub a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use any Background Technology incorporated in the Deliverables as part of the TravelHub App.

clauses.title: Intellectual property
clauses.text: TravelHub retains all rights in Customer Data.

clauses.title: Warranties
clauses.text: AtliQ warrants that the Services shall be performed in a professional manner consistent with generally accepted industry standards and that the Deliverables will materially conform to Schedule A for sixty (60) days after Acceptance.

clauses.title: Warranties
clauses.text: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET OUT IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY OTHER WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED.

clauses.title: Limitation of liability
clauses.text: Neither Party shall be liable for indirect, consequential, special or punitive damages or loss of profits.

clauses.title: Limitation of liability
clauses.text: Each Party's total liability arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, except for breach of confidentiality or wilful misconduct.

clauses.title: Indemnification
clauses.text: AtliQ shall defend and indemnify TravelHub against third-party claims alleging that the Deliverables infringe any intellectual property right.

clauses.title: Indemnification
clauses.text: TravelHub shall defend and indemnify AtliQ against third-party claims arising from Customer Data or TravelHub's use of the Deliverables in breach of applicable law.

clauses.title: Data protection
clauses.text: AtliQ shall process personal data only on TravelHub's documented instructions and in compliance with Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data and, where applicable, the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law.

clauses.title: Data protection
clauses.text: AtliQ shall not transfer Customer Data outside the TravelHub cloud environment without prior written approval.

clauses.title: Governing law and jurisdiction
clauses.text: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Emirate of Dubai and the applicable federal laws of the United Arab Emirates.

clauses.title: Governing law and jurisdiction
clauses.text: The courts of the Emirate of Dubai (onshore Dubai Courts) shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

clauses.title: General - Non-solicitation
clauses.text: Non-solicitation. During the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter, neither Party shall solicit for employment any employee of the other Party directly involved in the Services.

clauses.title: General - Assignment
clauses.text: Assignment. Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except to an Affiliate or successor in a merger.

clauses.title: General - Publicity
clauses.text: Publicity. AtliQ may list TravelHub as a customer on its website with TravelHub's prior approval.

clauses.title: General - Entire Agreement
clauses.text: Entire Agreement. This Agreement and its Schedules constitute the entire agreement of the Parties.

clauses.title: General - Notices
clauses.text: Notices. Notices to TravelHub shall be sent to Ms. Nadia Rahman, Co-founder; notices to AtliQ shall be sent to its President.

clauses.title: Deliverables and indicative timeline
clauses.text:
| Phase | Deliverable | Indicative completion |
| 1 | Data audit, feature design, ranking objective sign-off | Week 3 |
| 2 | Itinerary Personalization Engine v1 (staging) | Week 9 |
| 3 | Partner Hotel Ranking Module v1 — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Jeddah | Week 14 |
| 4 | Partner Performance Dashboard; production launch; model ops handover | Week 18 |
Acceptance criteria: offline ranking uplift (NDCG@10) of at least 10% over TravelHub's current rule-based sort; p95 API latency under 250 ms.

clauses.title: Preamble
clauses.text:
*(Client draft received 2026-09-10 via Dhaval's email. Client's paper — AtliQ has not yet marked up.)*
Harrington Health Systems, Inc. — Contract No. HHS-IT-2026-0193
Form: HHS Vendor MPSA (Rev. 07/2026)
This Master Professional Services Agreement (together with all Exhibits, Statements of Work and amendments hereto, this "Agreement") is entered into as of the date of the last signature below (the "Effective Date") by and between Harrington Health Systems, Inc., a Texas nonprofit corporation with its principal place of business at 6400 Fannin Street, Suite 1800, Houston, Texas 77030 ("Harrington" or "Client"), and AtliQ Inc, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("Contractor"). Client and Contractor are each a "Party" and collectively the "Parties."

clauses.title: Recitals
Definitions
clauses.text: "Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Applicable Law" means all federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations, ordinances and binding guidance applicable to a Party or the Services, including HIPAA, the HITECH Act, the Texas Medical Records Privacy Act (Tex. Health & Safety Code ch. 181), and the Anti-Kickback Statute.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Business Associate Agreement" or "BAA" means the business associate agreement attached hereto as Exhibit D.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Client Materials" means all data, information, systems access, documents and other materials furnished by or on behalf of Client.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Contractor Personnel" means all employees, agents, subcontractors and independent contractors of Contractor or its subcontractors who perform any portion of the Services.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Deliverables" means all work product, documentation, software, code, models, reports, dashboards, data pipelines, configurations and other materials prepared, developed or delivered by or on behalf of Contractor under this Agreement, in whole or in part.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Delivery Date" means each date for delivery or completion of a Deliverable or Milestone set forth in an applicable SOW.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Fees" means the amounts payable to Contractor as set forth in an SOW.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Losses" means any and all losses, damages, liabilities, deficiencies, claims, actions, judgments, settlements, interest, awards, penalties, fines, costs or expenses of whatever kind, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "PHI" has the meaning given to "protected health information" under 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Pre-Existing Materials" means any software, tools, libraries, frameworks, templates, methodologies, accelerators, know-how and other materials owned or licensed by Contractor prior to the Effective Date or developed independently of this Agreement.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Services" means the services described in Article 2 and in each SOW.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "SOW" means a statement of work executed by the Parties that references this Agreement.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Total Contract Value" means the aggregate Fees payable under this Agreement and all SOWs issued hereunder, which as of the Effective Date is Two Hundred Ten Thousand U.S. Dollars ($210,000.00).

clauses.title: Services - Scope
clauses.text: Scope. Contractor shall perform the Services described in the initial SOW attached as Exhibit A (the "Initial SOW"), which include: (a) design and build of a cloud data platform consolidating data from Client's electronic health record, patient accounting, scheduling and workforce management systems; (b) development of operational dashboards for bed management, emergency department throughput, operating room utilization and staffing; (c) a readmission-risk predictive model for use by Client's care management team; and (d) knowledge transfer to Client's Enterprise Analytics department.

clauses.title: Services - Additional SOWs
clauses.text: Additional SOWs. The Parties may from time to time execute additional SOWs. Each SOW shall be governed by this Agreement. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and an SOW, this Agreement shall control unless the SOW expressly states the specific Section of this Agreement it is intended to modify.

clauses.title: Services - Standards of Performance
clauses.text: Standards of Performance. Contractor shall perform the Services in a diligent, professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the highest standards of the industry, and in compliance with Applicable Law and Client's policies made available to Contractor, as updated from time to time.

clauses.title: Services - Contractor Personnel
clauses.text: Contractor Personnel. Contractor shall assign qualified Contractor Personnel. Client may, in its sole discretion, request removal of any Contractor Personnel, and Contractor shall promptly replace such individual at no additional cost to Client. Contractor Personnel accessing Client facilities or systems shall complete Client's background check, drug screening, immunization and compliance training requirements.

clauses.title: Services - Subcontracting
clauses.text: Subcontracting. Contractor shall not subcontract any portion of the Services without Client's prior written consent. Contractor shall remain fully responsible for any subcontractor's performance.

clauses.title: Services - Client Cooperation
clauses.text: Client Cooperation. Client shall use reasonable efforts to provide Contractor with access to Client Materials reasonably necessary for the performance of the Services.

clauses.title: Services - Change Orders
clauses.text: Change Orders. No change in the scope of Services shall be binding unless set forth in a written change order executed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

clauses.title: Acceptance
clauses.text: Client shall have thirty (30) days following delivery of each Deliverable to test and evaluate such Deliverable against the acceptance criteria in the applicable SOW.

clauses.title: Acceptance
clauses.text: If Client determines that a Deliverable does not conform, Client shall notify Contractor, and Contractor shall correct the non-conformity at no cost within ten (10) business days. Client may repeat the acceptance process until the Deliverable conforms, or may, at its option, reject the Deliverable and receive a refund of all Fees paid in respect thereof.

clauses.title: Acceptance
clauses.text: Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use in production, by payment, or by the passage of time.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Fees
clauses.text: Fees. Client shall pay Contractor the Fees set forth in each SOW. Fees are firm and fixed and shall not be increased during the term of the applicable SOW.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Invoices
clauses.text: Invoices. Contractor shall invoice Client monthly in arrears for Deliverables accepted in the preceding month. Each invoice shall reference the Contract No. and SOW number, and be submitted through Client's supplier portal. Invoices not submitted within ninety (90) days after acceptance shall be deemed waived.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Payment Terms
clauses.text: Payment Terms. Client shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within ninety (90) days after Client's receipt thereof.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Disputed Amounts
clauses.text: Disputed Amounts. Client may withhold payment of any amount it disputes in good faith. Contractor shall continue performing the Services during the pendency of any dispute.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Set-off
clauses.text: Set-off. Client may set off against any amount owed to Contractor any amount owed by Contractor to Client under this Agreement or any other agreement.

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Expenses
clauses.text: Expenses. Client shall reimburse only pre-approved, reasonable travel expenses incurred in accordance with Client's Vendor Travel Policy (Exhibit C).

clauses.title: Fees, invoicing and payment - Taxes
clauses.text: Taxes. Client is exempt from certain sales and use taxes and shall provide an exemption certificate upon request. Contractor shall be responsible for all taxes based on its income or personnel.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Term
clauses.text: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for three (3) years, unless earlier terminated as provided herein. Each SOW shall remain in effect for the period stated therein.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Termination for Cause
clauses.text: Termination for Cause. Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW upon written notice if the other Party materially breaches this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after written notice thereof.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Termination for Convenience
clauses.text: Termination for Convenience. Client may terminate this Agreement or any SOW, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Contractor. Upon such termination, Client's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by Client prior to the effective date of termination; Client shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Termination for Regulatory Reasons
clauses.text: Termination for Regulatory Reasons. Client may terminate immediately if Contractor or any Contractor Personnel is excluded from participation in any federal health care program.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Effect of Termination
clauses.text: Effect of Termination. Upon expiration or termination, Contractor shall (a) immediately deliver to Client all Deliverables, whether complete or incomplete, and all Client Materials; (b) provide transition assistance as reasonably requested by Client for up to ninety (90) days at the rates in the applicable SOW; and (c) certify in writing the return or destruction of all PHI in accordance with the BAA.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Survival
clauses.text: Survival. Articles 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 15 shall survive expiration or termination.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: "Confidential Information" means all non-public information disclosed by a Party, including business plans, financial information, patient information, trade secrets and Client Materials.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: Each Party shall (a) hold the other Party's Confidential Information in strict confidence, (b) use it only to perform or receive the Services, and (c) disclose it only to those employees and contractors with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: The foregoing obligations shall not apply to information that (a) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving Party; (b) was rightfully known without restriction prior to disclosure; (c) is rightfully received from a third party without restriction; or (d) is independently developed without use of the disclosing Party's Confidential Information.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: A receiving Party may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, provided it gives prompt prior notice (where legally permitted) and cooperates in seeking protective treatment.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: Contractor acknowledges that any breach of this Article may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be inadequate, and that Client shall be entitled to injunctive relief without the posting of bond.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Work Made for Hire
clauses.text: Work Made for Hire. All Deliverables shall be deemed "works made for hire" as defined in the U.S. Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. § 101, and shall be the sole and exclusive property of Client from creation.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Assignment
clauses.text: Assignment. To the extent any Deliverable, or any Pre-Existing Materials incorporated into or necessary for the use of any Deliverable, does not qualify as a work made for hire, Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers and conveys to Client all right, title and interest therein, including all intellectual property rights, without further consideration.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Further Assurances
clauses.text: Further Assurances. Contractor shall execute such documents and take such actions as Client may reasonably request to perfect, register or enforce Client's rights under this Article, and hereby appoints Client as its attorney-in-fact for such purpose.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Moral Rights
clauses.text: Moral Rights. To the extent permitted by law, Contractor waives, and shall cause Contractor Personnel to waive, all moral rights in the Deliverables.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Client Materials
clauses.text: Client Materials. All Client Materials are and shall remain the sole property of Client. Nothing in this Agreement grants Contractor any right in Client Materials except the limited right to use them to perform the Services.

clauses.title: Intellectual property - Third-Party Components
clauses.text: Third-Party Components. Contractor shall not incorporate any open-source or third-party software into any Deliverable without Client's prior written approval.

clauses.title: Representations and warranties
clauses.text: Each Party represents and warrants that it is duly organized, validly existing and in good standing, and has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.

clauses.title: Representations and warranties
clauses.text: Contractor further represents and warrants that: (a) the Services shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; (b) the Deliverables shall conform to the specifications in the applicable SOW for a period of twelve (12) months following acceptance; (c) the Deliverables shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any third-party intellectual property right; (d) the Deliverables shall not contain any virus, malicious code, time bomb or disabling device; (e) neither Contractor nor any Contractor Personnel is excluded, debarred or suspended from any federal health care program; and (f) Contractor shall comply with all Applicable Law.

clauses.title: Representations and warranties
clauses.text: Contractor shall, at Client's option, re-perform any non-conforming Services or refund the Fees paid therefor.

clauses.title: Indemnification - By Contractor
clauses.text: By Contractor. Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client, its Affiliates, and their respective trustees, directors, officers, employees, medical staff, agents, successors and assigns (the "Client Indemnitees") from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement or the BAA by Contractor, (c) any claim that a Deliverable infringes any third-party intellectual property right, or (d) any act or omission of Contractor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any Client Indemnitee.

clauses.title: Indemnification - By Client
clauses.text: By Client. To the extent permitted by law, Client shall indemnify Contractor against third-party claims to the extent arising from Client's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

clauses.title: Indemnification - Procedure
clauses.text: Procedure. The indemnified Party shall give prompt written notice of any claim, provided that failure to do so shall not relieve the indemnifying Party of its obligations except to the extent materially prejudiced. Client shall have the right to participate with counsel of its choice at Contractor's expense. Contractor shall not settle any claim without Client's prior written consent.

clauses.title: Limitation of liability - Exclusion of Consequential Damages
clauses.text: Exclusion of Consequential Damages. IN NO EVENT SHALL CLIENT BE LIABLE TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, EXEMPLARY OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

clauses.title: Limitation of liability - Cap on Client Liability
clauses.text: Cap on Client Liability. CLIENT'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID BY CLIENT TO CONTRACTOR UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.

clauses.title: Limitation of liability - Contractor Liability
clauses.text: Contractor Liability. NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE CONTRACTOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING CONTRACTOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF THE BAA, OR ANY DATA SECURITY INCIDENT.

clauses.title: Delay; liquidated damages - Time of the Essence
clauses.text: Time of the Essence. Time is of the essence with respect to each Delivery Date.

clauses.title: Delay; liquidated damages - Liquidated Damages
clauses.text: Liquidated Damages. The Parties acknowledge that Client's damages from delay would be difficult to ascertain. Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.

clauses.title: Delay; liquidated damages - Cumulative Remedies
clauses.text: Cumulative Remedies. Liquidated damages under this Article are in addition to and not in lieu of Client's right to recover its actual damages, to terminate this Agreement for cause, and to exercise any other right or remedy available at law or in equity. Client may deduct liquidated damages from any amounts otherwise due to Contractor.

clauses.title: Delay; liquidated damages - Notice of Delay
clauses.text: Notice of Delay. Contractor shall notify Client in writing within two (2) business days of becoming aware of any circumstance that may delay any Delivery Date, together with a recovery plan. Such notice shall not relieve Contractor of its obligations under this Article.

clauses.title: Data protection and security - HIPAA
clauses.text: HIPAA. Contractor shall comply with the BAA attached as Exhibit D, which is incorporated herein by reference. In the event of conflict between this Agreement and the BAA with respect to PHI, the BAA shall control.

clauses.title: Data protection and security - Security Program
clauses.text: Security Program. Contractor shall maintain a written information security program consistent with NIST SP 800-53 moderate baseline, including encryption of PHI at rest and in transit, multi-factor authentication, and logging and monitoring of access.

clauses.title: Data protection and security - Security Incidents
clauses.text: Security Incidents. Contractor shall notify Client of any actual or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Client data within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery and shall bear all costs of investigation, notification, credit monitoring and remediation.

clauses.title: Data protection and security - Offshore Restrictions
clauses.text: Offshore Restrictions. No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States without Client's prior written consent. Any Contractor Personnel located outside the United States shall access only de-identified data within Client-controlled environments.

clauses.title: Data protection and security - Audit
clauses.text: Audit. Client or its designee may audit Contractor's compliance with this Article upon ten (10) days' notice, no more than once annually except following a security incident.

clauses.title: Insurance
clauses.text: Contractor shall maintain, at its own expense, with carriers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best: (a) commercial general liability of $2,000,000 per occurrence; (b) professional liability/errors and omissions of $5,000,000 per claim; (c) cyber liability of $5,000,000 per claim; (d) workers' compensation as required by law; and (e) umbrella liability of $5,000,000.

clauses.title: Insurance
clauses.text: Client shall be named as additional insured on the CGL and umbrella policies. Contractor shall furnish certificates of insurance prior to commencing the Services.

clauses.title: Governing law and dispute resolution - Governing Law
clauses.text: Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Texas, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

clauses.title: Governing law and dispute resolution - Escalation
clauses.text: Escalation. The Parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through escalation to their respective executive sponsors for a period of thirty (30) days.

clauses.title: Governing law and dispute resolution - Venue
clauses.text: Venue. Any action arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Harris County, Texas, and each Party irrevocably submits to the personal jurisdiction of such courts.

clauses.title: Governing law and dispute resolution - Jury Waiver
clauses.text: Jury Waiver. EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES ITS RIGHT TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.

clauses.title: General provisions - Independent Contractor
clauses.text: Independent Contractor. Contractor is an independent contractor. Nothing herein creates an employment, partnership, joint venture or agency relationship.

clauses.title: General provisions - Assignment
clauses.text: Assignment. Contractor may not assign or transfer this Agreement, by operation of law or otherwise, without Client's prior written consent. Client may assign this Agreement to any Affiliate or successor without consent.

clauses.title: General provisions - Records and Audit
clauses.text: Records and Audit. Contractor shall maintain complete and accurate records relating to the Services for six (6) years and shall make them available to Client and to the Secretary of HHS as required by 42 U.S.C. § 1395x(v)(1)(I).

clauses.title: General provisions - Non-Exclusivity
clauses.text: Non-Exclusivity. This Agreement is non-exclusive. Client may engage other contractors for similar services.

clauses.title: General provisions - Publicity
clauses.text: Publicity. Contractor shall not use Client's name, logo or trademarks without Client's prior written consent.

clauses.title: General provisions - Force Majeure
clauses.text: Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that a Party affected shall give prompt notice and use diligent efforts to resume performance. Force majeure shall not excuse Contractor's obligations under Article 12 or its business continuity obligations.

clauses.title: General provisions - Notices
clauses.text: Notices. Notices shall be in writing and delivered by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier, or certified mail to the addresses above: if to Client, Attn: Dr. Rebecca Lowe, Chief Information Officer, with a copy to the Office of General Counsel; if to Contractor, Attn: President.

clauses.title: General provisions - Severability
clauses.text: Severability. If any provision is held invalid, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force.

clauses.title: General provisions - Waiver
clauses.text: Waiver. No waiver shall be effective unless in writing. No failure or delay in exercising any right shall operate as a waiver.

clauses.title: General provisions - Order of Precedence
clauses.text: Order of Precedence. In the event of conflict: (a) the BAA (as to PHI); (b) this Agreement; (c) the applicable SOW; (d) other Exhibits.

clauses.title: General provisions - Entire Agreement
clauses.text: Entire Agreement. This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement of the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior agreements. Contractor's quotes, invoices, click-through or shrink-wrap terms shall have no effect.

clauses.title: General provisions - Counterparts; Electronic Signatures
clauses.text: Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

clauses.title: Exhibits
clauses.text:
- Exhibit A — Initial Statement of Work (Enterprise Clinical & Operational Analytics Platform, Phase 1)
- Exhibit B — Client Information Security Requirements
- Exhibit C — Vendor Travel Policy
- Exhibit D — Business Associate Agreement

findings.whyItMatters: AtliQ Inc sub-contracts all delivery to AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd under the intercompany agreement (atliq_entities.md). Without consent written into the contract, the normal delivery model is a breach.

findings.whyItMatters: Karandeep's checklist: 'LDs → cap it. never open ended.' AtliQ's standard (Acme, Northwind, Trustline) is 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone, with no LDs for client-caused delay. This one runs daily on the whole contract value.

citation.quote: Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.

findings.whyItMatters: Liquidated damages are meant to be the agreed price of delay. Here the client can claim them and its actual losses as well, so the 'cap' on delay exposure disappears.

clauses.text: The Customer shall pay correctly rendered and undisputed invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt.

clauses.title: Charges and payment
clauses.text: The Customer may set off against any sums owed to the Supplier any amount owed by the Supplier to the Customer or any member of the Brightwater Group.

clauses.title: Acceptance
clauses.text: Each Deliverable shall be subject to acceptance tests determined by the Customer. The Customer shall notify the Supplier of acceptance or rejection within fifteen (15) Working Days of delivery.

clauses.title: Acceptance
clauses.text: If a Deliverable fails its acceptance tests, the Supplier shall remedy the failure and resubmit within ten (10) Working Days, at no additional charge.

clauses.title: Delay and liquidated damages
clauses.text: If the Supplier fails to achieve any Key Date, the Supplier shall pay to the Customer liquidated damages in the amount of one per cent (1%) of the Contract Value for each day or part day by which the relevant Key Date is missed.

clauses.title: Delay and liquidated damages
clauses.text: Liquidated damages under clause 9.1 shall be payable in addition to any other right or remedy available to the Customer under this Agreement or at law, and the Customer may deduct such liquidated damages from any sums due to the Supplier.

clauses.title: Delay and liquidated damages
clauses.text: The Supplier acknowledges that the liquidated damages set out in this clause 9 are proportionate to the Customer's legitimate interest in the timely delivery of the Services.

clauses.title: Personnel
clauses.text: The Supplier shall ensure that all personnel engaged in the Services are suitably skilled, have passed background checks in accordance with the Brightwater Group Vendor Screening Standard, and comply with the Customer's security policies.

clauses.title: Personnel
clauses.text: The Customer may require the removal of any Supplier personnel whose conduct is, in the Customer's reasonable opinion, unsatisfactory.

clauses.title: Intellectual property
clauses.text: All intellectual property rights in the Deliverables shall vest in the Customer on creation. The Supplier hereby assigns all such rights to the Customer with full title guarantee.

clauses.title: Intellectual property
clauses.text: The Supplier retains ownership of its pre-existing materials and grants the Customer and the Brightwater Group a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use any such materials incorporated in the Deliverables.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: The Supplier shall keep confidential all Customer Data and all information relating to the business of the Brightwater Group and shall not use it except for the performance of the Services.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: The Customer may disclose the Supplier's information to any member of the Brightwater Group, its regulators and its professional advisers.

clauses.title: Confidentiality
clauses.text: This clause 12 shall survive termination indefinitely.

clauses.title: Data protection and information security
clauses.text: The Supplier shall comply with all applicable data protection laws, including the Connecticut Data Privacy Act and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, and the Brightwater Group Information Security Schedule.

clauses.title: Data protection and information security
clauses.text: The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any security incident affecting Customer Data within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it.

clauses.title: Data protection and information security
clauses.text: The Supplier shall not process Customer Data outside the United States without the Customer's prior written consent.

clauses.title: Warranties
clauses.text: The Supplier warrants that the Services will be performed in accordance with Good Industry Practice and that the Deliverables will be free from material defects for a period of twelve (12) months after acceptance.

clauses.title: Indemnities and liability
clauses.text: The Supplier shall indemnify the Customer and each member of the Brightwater Group against all losses arising from (a) any breach by the Supplier of clauses 12 or 13, (b) any claim that the Deliverables infringe third-party rights, and (c) the negligence or wilful default of the Supplier.

clauses.title: Indemnities and liability
clauses.text: Neither party shall be liable for any indirect or consequential loss.

clauses.title: Indemnities and liability
clauses.text: Subject to clauses 9, 15.1 and 15.4, the Supplier's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed one hundred and fifty per cent (150%) of the Contract Value.

clauses.title: Indemnities and liability
clauses.text: Nothing in this Agreement shall limit liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud or any other liability which cannot be limited by law.

clauses.title: Termination
clauses.text: The Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice.

clauses.title: Termination
clauses.text: Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect if the other party commits a material breach which is not remedied within twenty (20) Working Days of notice.

clauses.title: Termination
clauses.text: On termination, the Supplier shall deliver all work in progress and Customer Data to the Customer.

clauses.title: Insurance
clauses.text: The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 and cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000.

clauses.title: Audit
clauses.text: The Supplier shall permit the Customer, the Brightwater Group internal audit function and any regulator to audit its compliance with this Agreement on reasonable notice.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: The Supplier shall not assign or subcontract without the Customer's prior written consent. The Customer may assign this Agreement to any member of the Brightwater Group.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties. The Supplier's standard terms shall not apply.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: No variation shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the parties.

clauses.title: General
clauses.text: A person who is not a party shall have no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any term, save that each member of the Brightwater Group may enforce clauses 12, 13 and 15.

clauses.title: Governing law and jurisdiction
clauses.text: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.

clauses.title: Governing law and jurisdiction
clauses.text: Each party irrevocably agrees that the courts of London, England shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.

clauses.title: Recitals
clauses.text:

clauses.title: Definitions

clauses.title: Preamble
clauses.text:
*(Text extracted from executed PDF. Stored: Karandeep's email attachments)*
CareBridge Clinics, Inc. — BAA No. CBC-BAA-2025-014
This Business Associate Agreement (this "BAA") is entered into as of October 6, 2025 (the "BAA Effective Date") by and between CareBridge Clinics, Inc., an Arizona corporation with its principal place of business at 2200 North Central Avenue, Suite 900, Phoenix, Arizona 85004 ("Covered Entity"), and AtliQ Inc, a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 101 College Road East, Suite 210, Princeton, New Jersey 08540 ("Business Associate"). Covered Entity and Business Associate are each a "Party" and together the "Parties."

clauses.title: Recitals
clauses.text:
A. Covered Entity and Business Associate are parties to a Master Services Agreement dated as of October 6, 2025 (together with its Statements of Work, the "Master Services Agreement"), under which Business Associate provides patient-scheduling analytics services to Covered Entity (the "Services").
B. In performing the Services, Business Associate may create, receive, maintain or transmit Protected Health Information on behalf of Covered Entity, and the Parties wish to comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act, and their implementing regulations at 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164 (collectively, "HIPAA").
NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree as follows:

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: Capitalized terms used but not defined in this BAA have the meanings given in HIPAA, including "Breach," "Data Aggregation," "Designated Record Set," "Individual," "Required By Law," "Secretary," "Security Incident," "Subcontractor" and "Unsecured Protected Health Information."

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Protected Health Information" or "PHI" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103, limited to information created, received, maintained or transmitted by Business Associate on behalf of Covered Entity.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "De-identified Data" means health information that has been de-identified in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b) and that is therefore not PHI.

clauses.title: Definitions
clauses.text: "Covered Entity Environment" means the cloud tenant, virtual desktops and other systems owned or controlled by Covered Entity and hosted in the United States, to which Covered Entity grants Business Associate access for the Services.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - Services
clauses.text: Services. Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Services under the Master Services Agreement, and as otherwise permitted or required by this BAA or as Required By Law.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - Minimum Necessary
clauses.text: Minimum Necessary. Business Associate shall limit its uses, disclosures and requests of PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.502(b).

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - Management and Administration
clauses.text: Management and Administration. Business Associate may use PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities, and may disclose PHI for those purposes if the disclosure is Required By Law, or Business Associate obtains reasonable written assurances from the recipient that the PHI will be held confidentially, used or further disclosed only as Required By Law or for the purpose for which it was disclosed, and that the recipient will notify Business Associate of any instance in which the confidentiality of the PHI has been breached.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - De-identification
clauses.text: De-identification. Business Associate may de-identify PHI in accordance with 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b) solely for the purpose of performing the Services. De-identified Data may be used only for the Services and not for any other client, product or purpose.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - Data Aggregation
clauses.text: Data Aggregation. Business Associate shall not perform Data Aggregation services unless expressly requested in writing by Covered Entity.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - No Sale; No Marketing
clauses.text: No Sale; No Marketing. Business Associate shall not sell PHI or use or disclose PHI for marketing purposes.

clauses.title: Permitted uses and disclosures - Prohibited Uses
clauses.text: Prohibited Uses. Business Associate shall not use or disclose PHI in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 if done by Covered Entity.

clauses.title: Location of phi and offshore access
clauses.text: Business Associate shall access, store and process PHI only within the Covered Entity Environment, and only through personnel of Business Associate who are located in the United States and who have been identified to Covered Entity by name in writing.

clauses.title: Location of phi and offshore access
clauses.text: Personnel of Business Associate or of any Subcontractor located outside the United States may access De-identified Data only, and only within the Covered Entity Environment or a secure environment approved in writing by Covered Entity. No PHI shall be accessed, stored or processed outside the United States.

clauses.title: Location of phi and offshore access
clauses.text: Business Associate shall maintain, and provide to Covered Entity on request, a current list of personnel with access to PHI.

clauses.title: Safeguards
clauses.text: Business Associate shall use appropriate administrative, physical and technical safeguards, and comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to electronic PHI, to prevent use or disclosure of PHI other than as provided by this BAA.

clauses.title: Safeguards
clauses.text: Without limiting Section 4.1, Business Associate shall (a) encrypt electronic PHI in transit and at rest consistent with guidance issued by the Secretary; (b) require multi-factor authentication for access to PHI; (c) maintain audit logs of access to PHI; and (d) provide HIPAA privacy and security training to its personnel with access to PHI before access is granted and annually thereafter.

clauses.title: Reporting - Breaches and Non-Permitted Uses
clauses.text: Breaches and Non-Permitted Uses. Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA, including any Breach of Unsecured PHI, without unreasonable delay and in no case later than five (5) business days after discovery. A Breach shall be treated as discovered as of the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to Business Associate.

clauses.title: Reporting - Content
clauses.text: Content. The report shall include, to the extent then known, the identity of each Individual affected, a description of the incident, the PHI involved, and the steps taken to mitigate it. Business Associate shall supplement the report as further information becomes available.

clauses.title: Reporting - Security Incidents
clauses.text: Security Incidents. Business Associate shall report successful Security Incidents in accordance with Section 5.1. The Parties agree that this Section constitutes notice of the ongoing existence of unsuccessful Security Incidents (such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts) for which no further notice is required.

clauses.title: Reporting - Mitigation and Notification
clauses.text: Mitigation and Notification. Business Associate shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect of a use or disclosure in violation of this BAA. Covered Entity shall determine whether notification to Individuals, the Secretary or the media is required and shall control the content of any such notification. Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable, documented costs of notification and credit monitoring to the extent the Breach was caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors, subject to Section 9.

clauses.title: Subcontractors
clauses.text: Business Associate shall ensure, in accordance with 45 C.F.R. §§ 164.502(e)(1)(ii) and 164.308(b)(2), that any Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on behalf of Business Associate agrees in a written business associate agreement to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate under this BAA, including Section 3.

clauses.title: Subcontractors
clauses.text: Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity in writing of any Subcontractor engaged in connection with the Services and shall remain responsible for the performance of its Subcontractors.

clauses.title: Individual rights - Access
clauses.text: Access. Within ten (10) business days of a request by Covered Entity, Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity as necessary for Covered Entity to meet its obligations under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.

clauses.title: Individual rights - Amendment
clauses.text: Amendment. Within ten (10) business days of a request by Covered Entity, Business Associate shall make any amendment to PHI in a Designated Record Set as directed by Covered Entity under 45 C.F.R. § 164.526.

clauses.title: Individual rights - Accounting
clauses.text: Accounting. Business Associate shall document disclosures of PHI and provide to Covered Entity, within fifteen (15) business days of request, the information required for Covered Entity to respond to a request for an accounting under 45 C.F.R. § 164.528.

clauses.title: Individual rights
clauses.text: Business Associate shall forward to Covered Entity within five (5) business days any request it receives directly from an Individual under this Section 7.

clauses.title: Other obligations - Books and Records
clauses.text: Books and Records. Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining compliance with HIPAA.

clauses.title: Other obligations - Covered Entity Obligations
clauses.text: Covered Entity Obligations. To the extent Business Associate carries out an obligation of Covered Entity under Subpart E of 45 C.F.R. Part 164, Business Associate shall comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to Covered Entity in the performance of that obligation.

clauses.title: Other obligations - Covered Entity Responsibilities
clauses.text: Covered Entity Responsibilities. Covered Entity shall (a) notify Business Associate of any limitation in its notice of privacy practices, any change in or revocation of an Individual's permission, and any restriction agreed under 45 C.F.R. § 164.522, to the extent it affects Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI; (b) disclose to Business Associate only the minimum PHI necessary for the Services; and (c) not request Business Associate to use or disclose PHI in any manner not permissible under HIPAA.

clauses.title: Other obligations - Assessment
clauses.text: Assessment. Upon thirty (30) days' written notice, and not more than once in any twelve (12) month period unless following a Breach, Covered Entity may request reasonable documentation (including a completed security questionnaire and relevant policies) to verify Business Associate's compliance with this BAA.

clauses.title: Liability
clauses.text: Each Party's liability arising out of or relating to this BAA, including any Breach, is subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability in the Master Services Agreement, under which aggregate liability for claims relating to a Breach or a violation of this BAA shall not exceed two (2) times the Fees paid or payable under the Master Services Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Term
clauses.text: Term. This BAA commences on the BAA Effective Date and continues until the Master Services Agreement expires or is terminated, subject to Section 10.4.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Termination for Cause
clauses.text: Termination for Cause. If either Party determines that the other has materially breached this BAA, it shall give written notice and a thirty (30) day period to cure. If the breach is not cured within that period, the non-breaching Party may terminate this BAA and the affected portions of the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Return or Destruction
clauses.text: Return or Destruction. On termination or expiry, Business Associate shall, within thirty (30) days, return to Covered Entity or destroy all PHI in its possession or in the possession of its Subcontractors, and certify the destruction in writing. If return or destruction is infeasible, Business Associate shall notify Covered Entity of the conditions that make it infeasible, extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI, and limit further uses and disclosures to those purposes that make return or destruction infeasible, for so long as Business Associate maintains the PHI.

clauses.title: Term and termination - Survival
clauses.text: Survival. Section 10.3 and the obligations of Business Associate with respect to any PHI retained under it survive termination.

clauses.title: General - Amendment
clauses.text: Amendment. The Parties shall amend this BAA as necessary to comply with any change in HIPAA. No other amendment is effective unless in writing and signed by both Parties.

clauses.title: General - Interpretation
clauses.text: Interpretation. Any ambiguity in this BAA shall be resolved to permit compliance with HIPAA. In the event of conflict between this BAA and the Master Services Agreement with respect to PHI, this BAA controls; in all other respects the Master Services Agreement controls.

clauses.title: General - No Third-Party Beneficiaries
clauses.text: No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Nothing in this BAA confers any rights on any person other than the Parties.

clauses.title: General - Governing Law
clauses.text: Governing Law. This BAA is governed by the laws of the State of Arizona, except to the extent preempted by federal law, and disputes shall be resolved as provided in the Master Services Agreement.

clauses.title: General - Counterparts
clauses.text: Counterparts. This BAA may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature.

clauses.text:
